claude_initial_call: CONTESTED; Occam alternative = pre-existing convertible subset is selected

audit.primary_source_citation: Gao Y, Souza-Fonseca-Guimaraes F, Bald T, ... Holzel M, Smyth MJ. "Tumor immunoevasion by the conversion of effector NK cells into type 1 innate lymphoid cells." Nat Immunol. 2017 Sep;18(9):1004-1015. PMID 28759001, DOI 10.1038/ni.3800. CARRIES AN AUTHOR CORRECTION: Nat Immunol 2024 May;25(5):925-926, PMID 38514890, DOI 10.1038/s41590-024-01799-9. Companion/secondary (NOT the primary for the intratumoural claim): Cortez VS et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003, PMID 28759002, PMCID PMC5712491. Hint source Dadi S et al. Cell 2016;164:365-377 (PMID 26806130) was checked and is MISATTRIBUTED for this claim - it concerns tissue-resident ILC1 and innate-like T cells in tumour immunosurveillance, and does not assert NK-to-ILC1 conversion.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Gao 2017 is CLOSED access (Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf status=CLOSED; EuropePMC/PMC return abstract only; nature.com Online Methods behind paywall; hal.science mirror returned Access Denied). I did NOT paraphrase the abstract: I reconstructed the design from the publisher's per-figure legend pages (nature.com/articles/ni.3800/figures/1-6), which returned legend text including recipient strains, route, timepoints and per-panel n, plus the full Author Correction text. The narrative Online Methods (sort gate purity, antibody clones, exact cell doses) remains unobtained. Cortez 2017 methods WERE fully obtained via PMC5712491. Park 2019 (eLife) full text obtained OA and archived.
audit.species: Mouse (C57BL/6 wild-type; Rag2-/-Il2rg(gc)-/-; CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics; Ncr1-iCre x Tgfbr2-fl/fl ["RII-FL"]; Ncr1-iCre x constitutively-active Tgfbr1 ["RI-CA-FL"]; Ncr1-iCre x Mcl1-fl). Limited correlative human data (GIST/melanoma). Counter-evidence source PMC13035902 is human colorectal cancer.
audit.what_was_measured: In mouse, in MCA1956 methylcholanthrene-induced fibrosarcoma, sorted splenic CD45.2+ NK cells were injected INTRATUMOURALLY into CD45.1+ tumour-bearing congenic hosts at day 14 and, at days 18-21, donor(CD45.2)-gated cells were scored by flow cytometry for the surface markers CD49a and CD49b plus intracellular Eomes, to count donor-derived CD49a+CD49b+Eomes+ "intILC1" and CD49a+CD49b-Eomes-int "ILC1" events, in n=3-4 recipient mice per timepoint (Fig 4d-g). In a parallel in-vivo arm, sorted NK cells from Ncr1-iCre Tgfbr2-fl/fl vs Tgfbr2-WT donors were transferred i.v. into MCA1956-bearing Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts at day 3 and the same CD49a/CD49b/Eomes marker composition was read at day 18 in n=6 recipient mice (Fig 4a-c), or transferred intratumourally into CD45.1+ hosts and read at day 21 in n=5-7 recipient mice (Fig 4h-j). Supporting readouts: RNA-seq of six matched triplicates of NK/intILC1/ILC1 sorted from the same MCA1956 tumour (n=6 tumours, Fig 1); Ki67 staining of donor-derived group 1 ILC subsets in the LIVER (not tumour) of Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts at 7 d (n=3 host mice) and 14 d (n=4 host mice) after NK transfer (Fig 3e); and in-vitro culture of sorted splenic NK cells with IL-15 +/- TGF-beta1 scored for the same CD49a/CD49b/Eomes markers in n=3 replicates (Fig 2c). No cell was ever individually tracked from an NK state to an ILC1 state.
audit.n: Fig 4a-c n=6 recipient mice; Fig 4d-g n=3-4 recipient mice per timepoint; Fig 4h-j n=7 (RII-WT) and n=5 (RII-FL) recipient mice; Fig 4k-l n=20 mice pooled from five experiments; Fig 3e n=3 (day 7) and n=4 (day 14) host mice; Fig 2a n=9 (d7), n=8 (d14), n=4 (d21); Fig 2b n=8; Fig 2c n=3 culture replicates; Fig 2d n=4/4/3; Fig 1 n=6 tumours (six matched sorted triplicates). Cortez 2017: typically 1-3 mice per genotype per timepoint, plus a single SMAD4-mutant human donor (n=1 person).
audit.n_unit: recipient/host mice (animals) for all transfer experiments; tumours for the RNA-seq (n=6 tumours); culture replicates for the in-vitro arm; 1 human donor for the Cortez SMAD4 polyposis patient. NOT cells.
audit.controls: (1) Congenic CD45.1 host / CD45.2 donor discrimination, so donor-derived output is separable from host cells. (2) Rag2-/-gc-/- recipients lack endogenous NK/ILC, removing host-derived ILC1 as a source. (3) Genetic requirement control: Tgfbr2-floxed (RII-FL) vs Tgfbr2-WT (RII-WT) donor NK cells, and Ncr1-cre/wt Cre-only controls. (4) In vitro: IL-15 alone vs IL-15 + TGF-beta1. (5) Functional arms used ctrl IgG vs anti-asGM1 depletion. NOTABLY ABSENT: no purity/contamination quantification of the sorted input NK gate reported in the legends; no non-tumour-bearing transfer control for the intratumoural arm; no clonal, barcode, or inducible genetic fate-mapping control. Ncr1-iCre is used only to delete genes, never as a fate map - and it could not serve as one, since ILC1s also express NKp46.
audit.methods_quote: Fig 3e legend (verbatim from publisher figure page): "Flow cytometry of NK cell-derived group 1 ILC subsets in the liver of Rag2-/-gc-/- mice at 7 d (n = 3 host mice) and 14 d (n = 4 host mice) after the transfer of NK cells, assessing Ki67 expression." || Author Correction (PMID 38514890), verbatim: "The data from the underlying experiments are believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable, respectively." and "The major finding of the paper that TGF-beta-driven conversion of NK cells into ILC1s is a novel mechanism by which tumors escape surveillance by the innate immune system remains unaffected. No concerns have been raised regarding other data in the paper." || Park et al. eLife 2019 (PMID 31393266) Results, verbatim from archived full text: "NK cells upregulated CD49a upon transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- mice, as previously reported" and, on Gao 2017 specifically: "There was no evidence presented that these Eomes- cells can circulate, though they proliferate when adoptively transferred into lymphocyte-deficient hosts. Moreover, it is not clear if these cells persist in the absence of tumor."
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION/EXPANSION OF A PRE-EXISTING CONVERTIBLE SUBSET WITHIN THE SORTED INPUT, which the design cannot exclude. All transfers were BULK and polyclonal - no barcoding, no clonal tracking, no inducible fate map - so a donor-derived CD49a+ output is equally consistent with outgrowth of a minor CD49a-low/intermediate or intILC1-primed contaminant inside the live sort gate as with conversion of the average NK cell. Three specific reasons this is not a pedantic worry: (i) the live sort gate cannot have included Eomes, which is intracellular and requires fixation, so the "CD49a-CD49b+Eomes+" input population was defined post hoc, not purified; the legends report no purity or contamination figure. (ii) The paper's OWN Fig 3 establishes that intILC1s have the GREATEST proliferative capacity (highest Ki67) among group 1 ILC subsets - differential proliferation is precisely the mechanism that converts a sub-1% contaminant into a dominant recovered population, and it is here documented by the authors themselves. (iii) For the Rag2-/-gc-/- arms (Figs 3e, 4a-c), CD49a upregulation is a documented GENERIC artefact of transfer into lymphopenic hosts, independent of tumour or TGF-beta - stated explicitly by Park et al. eLife 2019 as "previously reported" - so in those panels the ILC1-defining marker is confounded by lymphopenia-driven homeostatic proliferation and tissue lodging. The one arm that is genuinely resistant to the lymphopenia artefact is the intratumoural CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic transfer into immunocompetent tumour-bearing hosts (Fig 4d-g), and that arm rests on n=3-4 recipient mice and a purely marker-defined output. Secondary alternative: TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS - tumour ILC1s seeded from ILC precursors rather than from mature NK cells (see counter_evidence).
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, on three fronts. (1) RESEARCH-INTEGRITY COUNTER-EVIDENCE, which the initial call missed entirely: Gao 2017 carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) removing Figs 5e and 6d,e and Supplementary Figs 5c,d and 8c after an independent investigation commissioned by QIMR Berghofer concluded no evidence of the experiments' conduct or primary data could be confirmed and that the underlying data "are believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable." From the figure legends I retrieved, the removed panels are exactly the FUNCTIONAL consequence experiments - Fig 5e MCA carcinogenesis incidence in Ncr1-cre/RII-WT/RII-FL mice at 300 ug MCA; Fig 6d,e RM-1 prostate-cancer lung metastasis in RI-CA and Mcl1 models with anti-asGM1 vs IgG. So the "converted ILC1s fail to control tumours" half of the claim now rests on withdrawn data. Senior author Mark Smyth was found by QIMR Berghofer to have "seriously breached Codes relating to responsible research conduct," resigned in 2021, and has multiple retractions elsewhere (JCI, Clin Transl Immunology) attributed to fabricated figures. The correction asserts the conversion conclusion "remains unaffected," but that assertion is the authors'/journal's, not an independent replication. (2) ALTERNATIVE-ORIGIN COUNTER-EVIDENCE: PMID 41896575 / PMC13035902 (2026), human colorectal cancer, ~23,400 ILC/NK cells scRNA-seq from 11 patients (19 tissue samples), flow validation in 8 patients, OP9-DL1/Caco-2 differentiation assays from 24 patients - concludes tumour ILC1/trNK-like cells arise substantially from LOCAL DIFFERENTIATION OF IMMATURE PRECURSORS ("naive ILCs" and "early NK cells") seeding the tumour, not solely from conversion of mature NK. Its own evidence is INF_TRAJECTORY (RNA velocity/pseudotime) plus INF_INVITRO, so it weakens rather than refutes. Also PMID 35348580 (Ly49E separates liver ILC1s into embryo-derived and postnatal subsets) supports independent origins for the ILC1 pool. (3) SCOPE COUNTER-EVIDENCE: Park et al. eLife 2019 (PMID 31393266), the field's cleanest NK-to-ILC1 conversion study (Eomes-GFP reporter, Ncr1-iCre Eomes-fl/fl, WT:Tbx21-/- mixed BM chimeras), is an INFECTION model, not a tumour, and explicitly flags that Gao's tumour Eomes- cells were never shown to circulate or to persist in the absence of tumour. That same paper concedes that true Eomes fate mapping was not achievable (EomesCre unusable due to ubiquitous developmental expression) and that transfer of congenic NK cells before infection failed to yield recoverable cells - i.e., nobody in this literature has closed the loop.
audit.downstream_dependency: Named, concrete dependents: (1) Cortez VS et al., "SMAD4 impedes the conversion of NK cells into ILC1-like cells," Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003 (PMID 28759002) - the back-to-back companion paper, which cites Gao 2017 directly and frames its own SMAD4 phenotype as the same NK-to-ILC1 conversion axis, despite its own methods containing NO adoptive transfer and NO fate mapping (verified in PMC5712491 methods; its tumour readout is B16-F10 lung metastasis focus counts at day 15). (2) Souza-Fonseca-Guimaraes F, Cursons J, Huntington ND, "The NK cell-cancer cycle," Nat Immunol 2020 (DOI 10.1038/s41590-020-0728-z), co-authored by Gao 2017 authors, which embeds TGF-beta-driven NK-to-ILC1 conversion as a canonical evasion step. (3) The therapeutic rationale for combining TGF-beta/TGFbR1 blockade with NK-cell and CAR-NK adoptive therapy to "prevent NK dedifferentiation" rests on this claim. (4) Ducimetiere L et al., "Cxcr3 promotes protection from colorectal cancer liver metastasis by driving NK cell infiltration and plasticity," J Clin Invest 2025 (PMID 40168086, PMC12126236), which interprets intratumoural CD49a+ NK cells through the Gao conversion framework. (5) Interleukin-35 paper PMID 40610398 (Nat Commun 2025) explicitly models "ILC1-like conversion" of human NK cells on this precedent.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's verdict ("CONTESTED; Occam alternative is that a pre-existing convertible subset is SELECTED") lands on the right conclusion but for incomplete and partly wrong reasons, and misses the decisive fact. THREE CORRECTIONS. (a) Claude implicitly under-rated the evidence class. Gao 2017 is NOT a marker-similarity or trajectory paper. It contains a genuine OBS_TRANSFER: sorted CD45.2+ splenic NK cells injected intratumourally into CD45.1+ tumour-bearing immunocompetent congenic hosts, with donor-gated recovery of CD49a+ intILC1/ILC1 (Fig 4d-g), plus an OBS_GENETIC requirement (Tgfbr2-deleted donor NK cells fail to generate the ILC1 output, Fig 4h-j). Under the A.3 rubric that is the second-strongest class available, not an inferential one. The hint's suspicion that this was "phenotype shift in bulk populations" is wrong. (b) BUT Claude's alternative survives regardless, because transfer was bulk and polyclonal with no barcoding, no clonal tracking and no inducible fate map, and because the authors' own Fig 3 shows intILC1s are the most proliferative group 1 ILC subset - so selective outgrowth of a minor pre-existing contaminant in the sort gate is not excluded. Additionally, in the two Rag2-/-gc-/- arms the ILC1-defining marker CD49a is a documented generic artefact of transfer into lymphopenic hosts (Park eLife 2019). The hint's question "was any genetic fate-mapping tool used (Ncr1-cre, Eomes reporter)?" resolves as NO: Ncr1-iCre appears only as a gene-deletion driver, and it could not function as a fate map anyway because ILC1s also express NKp46. Searched specifically for true fate mapping of the NK-to-ILC1 axis and found none, in tumours or otherwise; the closest attempt (Park 2019) reports that Eomes-Cre fate mapping was not feasible. (c) THE FINDING NEITHER CLAUDE NOR THE HINTS FLAGGED, and the most important output of this audit: the primary source carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) that REMOVED Figs 5e and 6d,e and Supplementary Figs 5c,d and 8c because a QIMR Berghofer investigation could confirm no evidence the experiments were conducted and concluded the data "are believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable"; senior author Mark Smyth was found to have seriously breached research-conduct codes and has retractions in other journals for fabricated figures. Those removed panels are the tumour-incidence and metastasis-control readouts - i.e., the "and this lets tumours escape" half of the claim is now unsupported by published data, even though the conversion half is untouched by the correction. The claim should therefore be graded CONTESTED for a stronger reason than Claude gave: not merely that a cleaner alternative exists, but that the sole primary source is partially withdrawn for suspected fabrication, has never been replicated with lineage tracing by an independent group, and its intact conversion evidence rests on n=3-4 recipient mice in the one arm free of the lymphopenia artefact.
audit.notes: Provenance: full texts archived under /home/user/aaa/refs/ as T4_28759001.txt (Gao, abstract+metadata only - paywalled), T4_PMC5712491.txt (Cortez), T4_38514890.txt (Author Correction record), T4_PMC6703900.txt (Park eLife 2019, full OA text, 74,788 bytes). Gao figure legends were obtained from the publisher figure pages, reachable only by following the idp.nature.com redirect chain and appending ?error=cookies_not_supported. Distinguishing searched-vs-not per G3: I SEARCHED AND READ counter-evidence and found it (status FOUND). I SEARCHED for a true genetic fate-mapping study of the NK-to-ILC1 axis (two dedicated queries) and found none - that is a searched-and-absent result, not an assumption. I searched for and could not locate a Yulong Gao thesis in a UQ/QIMR repository that would have carried the verbatim Online Methods; the HAL mirror (hal-01765092) exists but returned Access Denied, and ResearchGate/Sci-Hub routes were not used. Hint accuracy: Gao 2017 and Cortez 2017 are correctly identified; Dadi 2016 is misattributed to this claim. Note also that Cortez 2017's phenotype is a GAIN of an ILC1-like gene signature upon Smad4 deletion, i.e. it is INF_MARKER on a knockout background rather than the canonical OBS_GENETIC pattern of "knock out gene, B fails to appear," and its methods contain no transfer and no fate mapping.
